title: JSON parameter descriptor format and gradual validation playbook
creator: Sana Mehta
description:
Context:
Redwood needs a lightweight, backward-compatible way to declare tool/function parameters that is both machine- and human-readable. Existing work on strict schema enforcement conflicts with real world model outputs and streaming behaviors; teams need a controlled path from permissive to strict validation without frequent breakages.

Goal:
Define a JSON parameter descriptor format (a compact superset of JSON Schema tailored for runtime tool calls) and a staged validation playbook that runtime, SDKs, and Console can adopt. The descriptor should enable: graded validation levels, repair suggestions, clear error codes, actionable telemetry, and graceful fallbacks to compatible parameter variants.

Key design principles:
- Compact descriptors: prefer concise type+shape hints instead of full JSON Schema for common cases (string, int, enum, object with required fields).
- Pseudotyping: allow authors to mark fields with "soft types" (e.g., "intish", "date-ish") that accept multiple lexical forms and provide conversion hints.
- Graded validation: three modes - permissive (no errors, only telemetry), warn (reject downstream call but surface structured warning and repair hint), strict (runtime returns structured error). Modes are configurable per-route/model and publishable as defaults in the model manifest.
- Repair hints: when validation fails, return a short, actionable "repair_hint" (human text) and a machine-readable recovery suggestion (coercion rule id).
- Error taxonomy: standardized error codes under namespace PARAM-*. Examples: PARAM-MISSING, PARAM-TYPE, PARAM-ENUM, PARAM-EXTRA, PARAM-REPAIR-APPLIED.
- Telemetry: emit param.validation.{result} (result in pass|warn|fail|repair) with fields: route, model_version, descriptor_id, validation_mode, error_codes.
- Backcompat: descriptors default to permissive if not present; SDKs must tolerate older parametrizations.

Descriptor format (example):
{
  "descriptor_id": "user-create-v1",
  "fields": {
    "email": {"type": "string", "format": "email", "required": true},
    "age": {"type": "intish", "min": 0},
    "signup_ts": {"type": "date-ish", "formats": ["iso8601", "unix-epoch"]},
    "plan": {"type": "enum", "values": ["free", "pro", "enterprise"], "default": "free"},
    "metadata": {"type": "object", "open": true}
  },
  "validation_defaults": {"mode": "warn"},
  "repair_rules": {"coerce_intish": "attempt parse int from digits in string"}
}

Notes on fields:
- "intish" and "date-ish" are pseudotypes implemented by runtime coercion helpers. They are intentionally tolerant during permissive/warn modes and treated strictly only in strict mode.
- "open": true allows extra keys under object; false fails with PARAM-EXTRA when strict.

Runtime behavior:
1) On incoming tool-call payload, runtime looks up descriptor by descriptor_id (route/model manifest fallback to built-in defaults).
2) Validate payload according to configured mode.
3) If a repair rule applies and mode != strict, attempt repair: log telemetry PARAM-REPAIR-APPLIED and include repaired_payload in trace (redacted where required).
4) If validation fails in warn or strict, return a structured error envelope: {"error_code": "PARAM-TYPE", "field": "age", "repair_hint": "Remove trailing text or provide integer", "suggested_payload": {"age": 27}}. For permissive mode, accept and emit telemetry only.

Error envelope and UX: (runtime -> client / SDK)
- top-level: code, message, field (optional), repair_hint (optional), suggestion_id (coercion rule id), documentation_url.
- Console should map codes to human-friendly explanations and link to descriptor docs.

Telemetry events and metrics:
- param.validation.start (descriptor_id, route, model_version, mode)
- param.validation.result (descriptor_id, result, error_codes[], latency_ms)
- param.repair.attempt (rule_id, success, before_summary, after_summary)
- param.fallback.invoked (fallback_descriptor_id)

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): spec + descriptor parser implemented in runtime; default descriptors for public tool catalog; permissive mode only; emit telemetry.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): SDK-side validator, console visualization of validation telemetry, warn mode opt-in for select customers.
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): strict mode gated rollout for internal tooling, migration guide for model authors and sample repair rules.

Migration guidance for model authors:
- Start by publishing descriptors with permissive mode and repair rules.
- Run telemetry for 2–4 weeks, fix common failure patterns, add coercion rules.
- Move route to warn and iterate; then consider strict for low-variance fields.

Security and privacy:
- Repaired payloads and before/after traces must be redacted for PII-sensitive fields based on descriptor metadata (e.g., "sensitive": true).
- Descriptors can mark fields requiring encryption in transit or at rest.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How expressive should pseudotypes be before they become a full schema language? Aim for small set (intish, floatish, date-ish, id-ish, enum, object) first.
- Storage: where do canonical descriptors live? Recommendation: model manifest + optional central descriptor registry in Console.
- Performance: runtime validation must add <1ms median overhead for typical small payloads; we will benchmark and micro-opt.

Deliverables:
- Spec document in Confluence (link below).
- Runtime descriptor parser + validator + telemetry hooks.
- SDK validation helpers with same descriptor compatibility.
- Console panels for validation telemetry and suggested repairs.
acceptance_criteria: Descriptor format doc published in Confluence and reviewed by PM and Design
Runtime implements descriptor lookup and permissive validation with telemetry emitted
SDKs provide same validation helpers and surface repair_hint for warn/strict modes
Console displays param.validation.result and top failing descriptors with example payloads (redacted)
End-to-end test coverage for repair rules and error envelopes
